To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Willmore energy is a Lyapunov functional and that its critical points are stable.

the Willmore energy of the flow is non-increasing, that the Willmore barycenter converges to the center of the round sphere, that the Will-more quadratic moment converges to zero, that the enclosed volume converges to the volume of the round sphere and that the averaged mean curvature converges to zero.

the barycenter of the evolving Willmore surface converges to the barycenter with a speed of at least O(E^2) for small energy E, and that the quadratic moment of a Willmore surface converging to a round sphere with small initial energy converges to zero with a speed of O(E^2).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the Willmore flow in the small energy regime.
stability properties of the Willmore flow in the regime of small initial energy.
the asymptotic stability properties of the Willmore flow.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Willmore evolution with small energy is very stable.
the Willmore energy is the only geometric quantity, which is stable under the flow.
the Willmore energy is a very stable quantity, if the surface is close to a round sphere.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Willmore evolution is a stable gradient flow with respect to the barycenter.
, in the case of small energy, the Willmore flow can be regarded as a perturbation of a standard round sphere.
the Willmore energy is the only geometric quantity that is stable in this setting.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Willmore evolution can be viewed as an asymptotic gradient flow for the Willmore energy, which allows us to apply the theory of gradient flows to the Willmore evolution.
stability bounds for the Willmore energy imply stability estimates for the shape of the surface.
the stability estimates for the Will-more flow can be derived from the stability analysis of the Willmore energy.
